title: Flyspeck Completes Full Machine-Checked Formal Proof of the 403-Year-Old Kepler Conjecture
whyItMatters: Resolved a 16-year refereeing crisis over Thomas Hales’s 1998 proof of Johannes Kepler’s 1611 sphere-packing conjecture by formally certifying every geometric lemma, tame graph, and 23,000 nonlinear inequalities in HOL Light and Isabelle.
summary: Announced complete on August 10, 2014 (published in Forum of Mathematics, Pi in 2017), Thomas Hales and an international 22-author Flyspeck collaboration completed the formal verification of the 1611 Kepler Conjecture—that no packing of equal spheres in 3D space exceeds the density π/√18 (~74.05%) of face-centered cubic packing. After Annals of Mathematics referees spent four years checking Hales’s 1998 proof and could only declare themselves “99% certain,” Flyspeck formalized the entire proof across HOL Light and Isabelle/HOL, combining symbolic proof automation with formally verified interval arithmetic and linear programming to eliminate all doubt.
technicalHighlights: Formally certified the complete proof of the 1611 Kepler Conjecture inside HOL Light and Isabelle/HOL.
Replaced unverified 1998 C++ code with machine-checked symbolic proofs covering tame-graph enumeration, ~23,000 nonlinear inequalities, and thousands of linear programs.
Turned a notorious “99% certain” refereeing crisis into a 100% kernel-verified mathematical theorem.
caveats: Human-led 11-year formalization effort assisted by HOL Light/Isabelle symbolic automation and certified solvers; included for apples-to-apples comparison with modern Lean formalizations.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved one of mathematics’ most famous verification crises—certifying the 403-year-old Kepler sphere-packing theorem.
scoreRationale.ripple: Proved that massive hybrid geometric + numerical proofs can be formally verified end-to-end, directly inspiring Lean sphere-packing formalizations.
scoreRationale.verification: 100% formally verified in HOL Light and Isabelle/HOL and published in Forum of Mathematics, Pi (2017).
scoreRationale.velocity: Required 11 years of global interactive formalization—an essential historical contrast to 2025–2026 AI formalization speeds.
